protocol_checks.vulnerability_mechanism: CONFIRMED: soup_message_headers_set_content_disposition() builds a caller-controlled Content-Disposition value through set_content_foo(); at the vulnerable revision replace_common()/append_common() accepts CR/LF unchanged, and both HTTP/1 request and response serializers append each stored name/value as '%s: %s\r\n', enabling header injection or response splitting. The live CVE.org record is PUBLISHED and GitLab issue 486 documents the same PoC-backed mechanism.
protocol_checks.atomic_bic: CONFIRMED: 732fcd4bb6899f8585f13789fadfc1de56c4a879 is the first history hit for set_content_foo() calling soup_message_headers_replace_common(hdrs, header_name, str->str); its exact hunk changes the previously validating replace() call to the unvalidated common-header fast path.
protocol_checks.immediate_parent_absence: CONFIRMED: the sole parent is 18ef5ed9166914334e0c107d251525a6d082722e, whose set_content_foo() still calls soup_message_headers_replace(); that public path rejects header values containing CR or LF even with G_DISABLE_CHECKS. The common sink exists in the parent, but Content-Disposition is not routed to it, so the vulnerable source-to-sink edge is absent.
